recentItems.title: FRED ALLEN: "The Ransom of Red Chief" with OSCAR LEVANT (1952) [UPGRADE!]
recentItems.description:
Upgraded video! This is a 25 minute segment from the anthology film O. Henry's Full House (1952), deftly directed by Howard Hawks, and just the right length for the story it's telling. Fred Allen and Oscar Levant play down-on-their-luck petty con artists who resort to kidnapping, only to find the parents of their quarry none too eager to get the boy back.  

Far and away Fred's best movie role, and quite possibly Levant's, too, since he's not reduced (for a change) to merely playing Oscar Levant, making superfluous sarcastic quips in the background of a musical whose plot had nothing to do with him (and didn't even pretend to.) 

Well worth watching if you haven't seen this before!

imdb: http://www.imdb.com/title/tt0044981/

recentItems.title: Lost WML Episode with Carl Reiner FOUND! (and future plans!)
recentItems.description:
Huge news, folks:  A What's My Line episode from 1967 surfaced in an eBay listing, and we managed to snag it.  Details in the video.  Sincere apologies for the awful sound quality-- I added subtitles to make sure folks can understand what I'm saying!

The new episode will be streamed on October 19th, 2025.  Details about the stream will only be found in the WML Facebook group, not on YouTube.  You'll just have to join if you want to know!

Immense thanks to Stan Taffel for all of his help, from handling the auction bidding itself, to doing his usual expert job transferring the film itself to digital.

recentItems.title: What's My Line - Happy Birthday, Bennett! [CLIPS VIDEO]
recentItems.description:
A short collection of WML clips acknowledging Bennett Cerf's birthday, just because today (May 25, 2019) marks the 121st anniversary of his birth.  He is still loved and missed, not just by fans of WML but by anyone who knows Bennett's historic contributions as a lifelong champion of both literature and the importance of humor in our lives.

recentItems.title: Judge For Yourself w FRED ALLEN (Jan 19, 1954?)
recentItems.description:
These shows are a real treat for Fred Allen fans, since they may never be shown on TV again due to the prominence of the cigarette sponsor, Old Gold.  As far as I'm concerned, any Fred Allen video is a precious Fred Allen video, since there's so very little outside of What's My Line.  But at least this handful of his shows was rerun once, so you can. . . Judge for Yourself!
